clue.text: Armistice arranged — 100 released, one after another

indicators.note: arranged says the remaining letters of the treaty word are set out in a new order
released says the letter for a hundred is let go from the word

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A truce is agreed and a hundred prisoners are freed in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'released' lets C go from ARMISTICE, leaving ARMISTIE, and 'arranged' reorders those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriatim is Latin-derived usage for taking points in sequence, each following the previous.

clue.text: Husband turning up? I have to be shifty

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to husband resources is to save them
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A suspicious wife wonders whether her husband appearing is a sign she must be sneaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a noun but is the verb, to conserve; 'turning up' reverses SAVE to EVAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shifty dodges straight answers, which is being evasive.

clue.text: Such characters aren't in good hands

definitions.text: Such characters aren't in good hands

parts.words: Such characters aren't in good hands
parts.note: characters are written letters and good hands are neat handwriting: letters from a scrawl cannot be read

explanation.definitionFit: Writing that cannot be deciphered is described as unreadable.

clue.text: Robber in Italian city pinching coin

indicators.note: pinching means the city name grips the coin inside it

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
P stands for a penny, a British coin

explanation.surface: A thief in an Italian city steals a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick TURPIN was a famous 18th-century English highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: The highwayman Dick Turpin held up coaches on English roads, a celebrated thief.

clue.text: Brussels sprouts their speciality?

parts.note: reads as growers of a vegetable, but Brussels is home of the European Common Market, so its growth is a commercial speciality

explanation.definitionFit: People who grow vegetables commercially for sale are called market gardeners in Britain.

clue.text: Spiteful women holding it back still

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled string is read in reverse
holding means the women contain the next word

parts.note: cats are spiteful women in old slang

explanation.surface: Catty women hold something back and keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts IT inside CATS for CITATS, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something static is motionless, not moving at all.

clue.text: 1,000 years in making, this training college

indicators.note: making signals the letters being made into something new

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A college boasts it took a millennium to build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges M, YEARS and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college that trains priests or ministers.

clue.text: Old historian understood America

parts.note: tacit means understood without being said
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: An ancient historian knew about the New World.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman writer of histories of the early empire.

clue.text: Case in which river god helped the farmer

indicators.note: in which places the river and god inside the case

parts.note: taken as written
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A tale of a god emerging from a river to lend a hand on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: R and THOR go inside CASE; the definition reads as '(one that) helped the farmer', the answer being the case in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy draught animal pulled wagons and ploughs for farm work.

clue.text: Fresh man on the line

definitions.meaning: an old Scots word applied to newly caught fish

explanation.definitionFit: Caller is a Scots word for fresh, of fish; also someone telephoning is on the line.

clue.text: Capital solution some might, say from a liar

indicators.note: some might say signals a sound-alike of the phrase before it

parts.note: Rome is a capital and an answer is a solution

explanation.surface: Someone claims a liar holds the key to an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: ROME ANSWER, said quickly, sounds like ROMANCER.
explanation.definitionFit: A romancer invents tall stories, a teller of fanciful untruths.

clue.text: Some sparring's ideally observed here

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sparring bouts are best watched from close quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators at a boxing match watch from seats beside the ring.

clue.text: Malay lord comes back, honoured by Indian dancing

indicators.note: comes back means the title is read backwards

parts.note: tuan is a Malay word for lord or master
CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A Malay nobleman returns and is feted with Indian dance.
explanation.walkthrough: TUAN reversed gives NAUT; CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautch is a traditional Indian performance by professional dancing girls.

clue.text: English town tops American poll

definitions.meaning: a town in the East Midlands of England
a bowler hat in US usage, worn on top of the head (poll)

explanation.definitionFit: Derby is an English place; a derby is an American bowler hat, covering the head.

clue.text: Appropriate churchman if getting wed fast in new arrangement?

indicators.note: new arrangement says the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quick wedding suits a clergyman well.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift was Dean of St Patrick's, Dublin; 'Appropriate' because swift also means fast, one of the anagram words.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, was a Dublin cathedral dean, a clergyman.

clue.text: Attacker got silver and gold out of work unit returning to ship

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: returning means the unit's name is read backwards

parts.note: an erg is a unit of work in physics
SS stands for steamship
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An aggressor wins medals and returns to his vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is one who strikes first, starting a fight.

clue.text: Give the Golf Club account of this birdie

parts.note: a spoon is an old wooden golf club
a bill is an account of charges

explanation.surface: A golfer asks the club to record a birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birdie' looks like golf scoring; here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoonbill is a wading bird with a flat broad beak.

clue.text: Sound quality in wise man a long time ago

indicators.note: in places the quality inside the wise man

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
tone is the quality of a sound

explanation.surface: A sage of ancient times had a fine voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period when tools were made from rock lies far in the past.

clue.text: Risk unaverted, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A danger that was not avoided, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is a venture involving hazard, so a risk.

clue.text: Six? 'Tis upside-down, or 9

definitions.note: refers to 9 across, someone paying a visit

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six

indicators.note: in a down clue upside-down means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about numbers that look different when inverted.
explanation.walkthrough: TIS reversed gives SIT. The definition is the answer to 9 across, someone who calls round.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who calls at the house is a guest coming to see you.

clue.text: For balance in attitude I must be in centre

indicators.note: must be in centre puts the letter in the middle of the word

parts.note: a pose is a physical attitude

explanation.surface: To keep balance, a dancer must hold a central stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise means steadiness or equilibrium.

clue.text: Add point to form? That's about right

indicators.note: about means the word goes round the next letter

parts.note: shapen is an archaic verb for to form

explanation.surface: A remark that sharpening one's form is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To sharpen a pencil is to give it a point.

clue.text: Dramatically presented the' old way first

indicators.note: first says the way comes before the old

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
aged means old

explanation.surface: A performance done in the traditional manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Staged means put on as a theatre production.

clue.text: One's concealed in hide to see finch

indicators.note: concealed in means the first part is placed within the hide

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
one is I, so one's is I'S, read as IS

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher hides in a blind to spot a finch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' suggests a birdwatching shelter but is SKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

clue.text: North European public schoolboys moving South

indicators.note: moving means one letter is shifted to a new place

parts.note: Etonians are boys at Eton College, an English public school
S is South

explanation.surface: Boys from an elite school relocate southwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The S moves from the end of ETONIANS to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: An Estonian comes from a Baltic state in northern Europe.

clue.text: Familiar state

definitions.meaning: to declare or hint at, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Intimate friends are close; to intimate something is to announce or make it known.

clue.text: Influenza almost took firm hold

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: gripped means took a firm hold

explanation.surface: Flu nearly took hold.
explanation.definitionFit: La grippe is an old name for flu.

clue.text: Most of the people in this part of the Balkans

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a race is a people

explanation.surface: Most of the population lives in this Balkan region.
explanation.walkthrough: THE loses its E to give TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace is a historical region spanning Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.

clue.text: Surface extended, obliquely

parts.note: a side is a surface
long means extended

explanation.surface: A surface was stretched out at a slant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelong look is cast sideways, at an angle.
